assets.descriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann anionische, kationische und nichtionische Tenside anhand ihres Aufbaus charakterisieren.
assets.descriptionEn: The learner can characterize anionic, cationic, and nonionic surfactants based on their structure.
assets.reason: The hydrophilic head / hydrophobic alkyl-tail model and the anionic, cationic and nonionic head-group distinctions agree with the complete goal. No definite chemical error is visible.
scientificChecks: The anionic example is an alkyl sulfate ester: R–O–S(=O)2–O− with Na+ shown separately. The negative charge is on oxygen, not a neutral sulfate group. The two S=O bonds and two S–O single bonds form a conventional valid sulfate-ester representation.
The cationic example shows N+ attached to one alkyl chain and three CH3 groups, hence four substituents; Cl− is a separate counterion. No fifth N bond or missing positive charge is visible.

The nonionic example is an ethoxylate R–O–(CH2–CH2–O)n–H. The repeat-boundary oxygen and terminal H are compatible with neutral ether/alcohol oxygen valences. Its polar, uncharged head is distinguished from the charged heads.
Water / oil arrows support amphiphilic affinity. They are not shown as a balanced chemical reaction or a claim that oil converts into water.

phone360.mainMotifs: Four columns remain separated. The large tail/head, minus, plus and uncharged polar head remain distinguishable without reading the chemical formulas.
phone360.estimatedPixels: Each column is approximately 84 px wide; the large head circles are about 35–39 px across and the plus/minus symbols about 17–22 px. Class headings are approximately 9–11 px high. The detailed formula subscripts are only approximately 3–5 px high.
phone360.essentialDetailVerdict: PASS for compact orientation to three head-group types. Detailed formula transcription and the polar/unpolar explanatory wording require enlargement; those are supplementary to the large repeated head/tail and charge motifs.

desktop680.mainMotifs: All four columns, head charges, alkyl chains, counterions and repeat-group formula can be inspected.
desktop680.estimatedPixels: Columns approximately 158–165 px wide; class headings approximately 18–21 px; formula characters approximately 11–14 px with smaller subscripts.
desktop680.essentialDetailVerdict: PASS; no cropping or clipping seen.

assets.representationStyleAge: Friendly bright comic pictograms combine with conventional structural formulas. This is appropriate for Gymnasial surfactant chemistry; the supplied packet does not identify an exact year, so no exact-grade claim is made.
boundedLimitations: The short drawn alkyl zigzags are schematic representatives, not a quantitative specification of a commercial surfactant chain length.
At 360 px this is an orientation image, not a legible chemical formula worksheet. No full mechanistic account of adsorption or micelles is implied.

assets.descriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann Funktionen von Enthärtern, Bleichsystemen, Enzymen und Hilfsstoffen erklären.
assets.descriptionEn: The learner can explain functions of softeners, bleaching systems, enzymes, and auxiliaries.
assets.reason: The four ingredient-function groups match the complete goal. Builder ion binding, oxidative bleaching, substrate-selective enzymatic breakdown and examples of auxiliaries are represented without a definite visible chemical error.
scientificChecks: Builder characters bind separately shown Ca2+ and Mg2+ hardness ions. This conveys sequestration/removal of hardness from solution rather than changing their charge or depicting a covalent molecular formula.

The peroxide O–O motif leads by an arrow to fading coloured stain and is explicitly labelled oxidation of coloured stains. It does not claim that peroxide is a surfactant, that bleaching is reduction, or that all organic material is simply dissolved.

Three enzyme characters act on labelled protein, fat and starch motifs, with smaller fragments. The caption specifies cleavage of matching substances, consistent with substrate-selective enzyme action. The food-like objects are substrate analogies, not chemical structural formulas.

The auxiliaries panel separates foam regulation, optical brighteners, fragrance and corrosion protection. The UV-in / blue-light-out arrows for optical brighteners convey fluorescence and keep it distinct from oxidative bleaching.

phone360.mainMotifs: All four panels and their functions remain visually distinguishable: hardness-ion capture, faded stain, three enzyme/substrate pairs, and foam/light/fragrance/shield motifs.
phone360.estimatedPixels: Panels approximately 84–88 px wide. Ingredient headings approximately 9–11 px high; the paired stained and pale cloths are about 33–39 px across. Fine auxiliary labels and lower captions are approximately 4–6 px high.
phone360.essentialDetailVerdict: PASS for function overview from main motifs. Small ingredient/example labels need enlargement; the image cannot support detailed reading of all auxiliaries at 360 px.

desktop680.mainMotifs: Ingredient groups, charge superscripts, bleaching arrow, enzyme rows and separate auxiliary arrows are inspectable and the captions are readable.
desktop680.estimatedPixels: Panels approximately 158–165 px wide. Group headings approximately 18–21 px high; captions approximately 11–13 px.
desktop680.essentialDetailVerdict: PASS; the essential before/after bleaching comparison and UV-to-blue fluorescence arrow remain separated.

assets.representationStyleAge: Approachable comic illustration with a household context and consistent line work. The metaphors are age-appropriate for Gymnasial chemistry and do not introduce extra assessment content.
boundedLimitations: A single overview cannot state the formulation-dependent presence of every ingredient; it should not be read as a claim that every detergent contains all four groups or every listed auxiliary.
The enzyme and builder characters are mechanism metaphors, not atomistic reaction diagrams.

assets.descriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann einfache MO-Diagramme (z. B. O2, N2) interpretieren und Bindungsordnung ableiten.
assets.descriptionEn: The learner can interpret simple MO diagrams (e.g. O2, N2) and derive bond order.
assets.reason: The O2 valence-MO occupation, ordering, electron counts and bond-order calculation are internally correct and directly serve the goal. A precise technical orbital diagram is appropriate here.
scientificChecks: Ascending O2 valence ordering is sigma2s, sigma*2s, sigma2pz, degenerate pi2px/pi2py, degenerate pi*2px/pi*2py, sigma*2pz. The sigma2pz lies below the bonding pi2p pair, as appropriate for the illustrated O2 example.
Electron arrows give (sigma2s)^2(sigma*2s)^2(sigma2pz)^2(pi2px)^2(pi2py)^2(pi*2px)^1(pi*2py)^1 and empty sigma*2pz: twelve valence electrons. Each occupied doubly filled box has opposite spin arrows.
The two degenerate pi* orbitals each contain one parallel unpaired electron. The statement of two unpaired electrons and paramagnetism agrees with the diagram.

Bonding occupation is 2+2+4=8 and antibonding occupation is 2+2=4; (8−4)/2=2 is correct. Omitting the cancelling occupied 1s core pair is a conventional valence-only simplification, not a wrong bond order.

phone360.mainMotifs: Energy direction, ordered boxes, paired versus single arrows, red/blue orbital classes, counts and the final bond order remain recognizable. The explanatory lines are still readable in the supplied actual 360 px image.
phone360.estimatedPixels: Orbital boxes approximately 20–22 px wide and 19–21 px high. Spin arrows approximately 12–15 px high. Main calculation lettering approximately 11–15 px high; orbital subscripts approximately 4–6 px.
phone360.essentialDetailVerdict: PASS for the core occupation and bond-order idea; detailed x/y/z subscript reading is the smallest element and may need enlargement. The critical single versus paired occupation is not encoded solely by tiny text.

desktop680.mainMotifs: Every orbital label, spin arrow, degeneracy pairing, electron total and calculation can be inspected.
desktop680.estimatedPixels: Boxes approximately 39–41 px wide and 36–40 px high; arrow shafts approximately 25–29 px high. Main calculation lettering approximately 22–28 px; smallest orbital subscripts approximately 8–12 px.
desktop680.essentialDetailVerdict: PASS; no clipping, contradictory count or ambiguous occupied box seen.

assets.representationStyleAge: A sparse technical diagram is warranted by the goal of interpreting MO diagrams. Soft background and blue/red coding maintain approachability; lack of a comic character is not a defect. The diagram is appropriate for the advanced Gymnasial chemistry described by the goal.
boundedLimitations: This is an O2 example, not a claim that N2 has the same 2p ordering. The goal says e.g. O2 or N2 and does not require both in one orientation image.
Paramagnetism is a correct direct consequence of the shown occupancy but is supplementary to deriving the bond order.

assets.descriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann an vorgegebenen Molekülpaaren mit gleicher Konstitution anhand ihrer räumlichen Anordnung begründen, ob Stereoisomerie vorliegt, und gegebenenfalls den passenden Stereoisomerietyp zuordnen.
assets.descriptionEn: The learner can use supplied pairs of molecules with the same constitution to explain from their spatial arrangements whether stereoisomerism is present and, where applicable, assign the appropriate type of stereoisomerism.
assets.reason: The supplied pairs have the same constitution within each pair and correctly illustrate conformers, enantiomers and E/Z diastereomers. No definite stereochemical inversion or valence error is visible.
scientificChecks: The Newman views show ethane with three H ligands on each carbon. The staggered view alternates front and back bonds; the eclipsed view aligns them with a slight display offset so that both front/back H labels remain visible. The curved arrows indicate rotation about the same single bond.

The central pair has C bonded to CH3, C2H5, Br and H. These are four distinct substituents. The Br wedges and H dashed bonds are mirrored left/right while the upper and lower substituents stay fixed, giving non-superposable enantiomers rather than identical planar drawings.

The alkene pair is 1,2-dichloroethene: each alkene carbon has a C=C bond and one H and one Cl single bond, satisfying carbon valence. The left Cl substituents are opposite (E/trans); the right Cl substituents are together (Z/cis). These are diastereomers, not mirror images.
The E/trans and Z/cis equivalence is used for this concrete symmetric H/Cl alkene. The image does not state that cis/trans and E/Z are interchangeable for every substituted alkene.

phone360.mainMotifs: Three coloured columns, rotatable Newman pair, mirror-separated tetrahedral pair and the opposite/same-side Cl arrangements remain distinguishable. Solid Br wedges and dashed H bonds remain visible as different bond styles.
phone360.estimatedPixels: Panels approximately 111–113 px wide. Category headings approximately 11–13 px high; atom circles approximately 10–16 px across, with atom/formula letters approximately 4–7 px high. E/trans and Z/cis labels approximately 7–8 px high.
phone360.essentialDetailVerdict: PASS for comparing the orientation motifs. Complete CH3/C2H5 transcription and the smallest Newman H letters require enlargement; different coloured substituent positions and bond styles carry the essential spatial distinction.

desktop680.mainMotifs: Front/back Newman bonds, four different central substituents, mirror line, wedge/dash bonds and all Cl/H positions can be inspected.
desktop680.estimatedPixels: Panels approximately 208–213 px wide; category headings approximately 23–25 px high; atom circles approximately 20–31 px across; atom/formula letters approximately 9–14 px.
desktop680.essentialDetailVerdict: PASS; no clipping or ligand overlap that changes identity seen.

assets.representationStyleAge: Friendly rounded panels and coloured atom tokens fit the visual landscape while the molecular conventions remain explicit. Appropriate for Gymnasial stereochemistry; this is an orientation overview rather than a stereochemical assessment task.
boundedLimitations: The slight drawing offset in the eclipsed Newman view is for legibility; it must not be used to read an exact non-zero torsion angle.
The image provides positive examples. It does not exhaust all stereoisomer classes or provide every non-isomer counterexample covered by the complete goal.
